description: Wire the new editor into OperatorWindow's two edit entry points for Slides items only, with the remove/save/refresh flow and live-name re-prime, leaving every other item type on AddServiceItemDialog. Depends on FEAT-002 (the window + RemoveRequested event + Result). This closes the feature end-to-end: opening a Slides service item now opens SlideServiceItemEditorWindow, and Save persists via the existing ServiceOrderManager.SaveAsync (JSON + SQLite mirror) and refreshes sidebar/center + re-primes the slide presentation cache.
steps: In WorshipPlayer.Presenter\Views\OperatorWindow.xaml.cs add `private bool TryOpenSlideServiceItemEditor(ServiceItem item)`: return false when item.Type != ServiceItemType.Slides, when _serviceOrderManager?.CurrentServiceOrder is null, or when any of _slidePresentationService/_mediaLibraryService/_templateService is null (so it safely falls back to the generic dialog). Otherwise construct `new SlideServiceItemEditorWindow(item, _serviceOrderManager.CurrentServiceOrder.Items, _slidePresentationService, _mediaLibraryService, _templateService) { Owner = this }`.

In TryOpenSlideServiceItemEditor subscribe `win.RemoveRequested += (_, __) => { removed = true; win.DialogResult = false; win.Close(); };` (local bool removed=false), then `bool saved = win.ShowDialog() == true;`. After ShowDialog, run on the dispatcher (Dispatcher.InvokeAsync async): if removed -> `int index = _serviceOrderManager.CurrentServiceOrder.Items.IndexOf(item); if (index >= 0) _serviceOrderManager.RemoveItem(index);` else if (!saved) return; else the window already copied back. Then `await SaveServiceOrderAsync(); await PrimeSlidePresentationCacheAsync(); RefreshServiceOrderList(); RefreshSlideSections();`. Return true.
At the TOP of EditSelectedServiceItem() (after the null/`display.Item == null` guards, before constructing AddServiceItemDialog) add `if (TryOpenSlideServiceItemEditor(display.Item)) return;`.

At the TOP of EditServiceItemDirect(ServiceItem item) (before constructing AddServiceItemDialog) add `if (TryOpenSlideServiceItemEditor(item)) return;`. Leave OpenSelectedItemSettings and all non-Slides paths unchanged.

Integration round-trip check: reuse/extend WorshipPlayer.Tests\SlideServiceItemEditorModelTests.cs to assert end-to-end persistence through ServiceOrderManager for a Slides item carrying all additive fields + an AutoAdvanceSettings with AutoAdvanceGoTo=SpecificItem + GoToItemId (save -> reload from the JSON file -> fields equal; and the ServiceOrders.DataJson mirror row contains them). This verifies the host save path without WPF. (If FEAT-001 already covers the manager round-trip + mirror, extend it with the SpecificItem/GoToItemId when-complete assertion rather than duplicating.)

Confirm the three real service-order JSON files + demo files still deserialize without error via ServiceOrderManager.LoadAsync (add a test that loads each real file found under the worktree's ServiceOrders path if present, asserting non-null and no throw).
acceptance_criteria: Double-clicking / Edit on a Slides service item opens SlideServiceItemEditorWindow; every other item type still opens AddServiceItemDialog unchanged.
When services are unavailable, TryOpenSlideServiceItemEditor returns false and the generic dialog is used (no crash).

Remove raises the host's RemoveRequested subscriber, which sets DialogResult=false so remove and save-and-close are mutually exclusive; the host runs RemoveItem -> SaveServiceOrderAsync -> refresh exactly once.
Save-and-close persists via ServiceOrderManager.SaveAsync and the host re-primes PrimeSlidePresentationCacheAsync then RefreshServiceOrderList + RefreshSlideSections so live names update.
The additive fields round-trip through the JSON file and the ServiceOrders.DataJson SQLite mirror; the three real service JSONs + demos still load.
`dotnet build WorshipPlayer.UI/WorshipPlayer.UI.csproj -c Debug` succeeds and `dotnet test` passes.
verification: Run: dotnet build WorshipPlayer.UI/WorshipPlayer.UI.csproj -c Debug  (from the worktree root) — expect Build succeeded.
Run: dotnet test  — expect the full suite green, including the round-trip/mirror/legacy-load assertions.
Confirm no bin/obj deletion or clean was performed during verification.
findings:
DONE. Build (WorshipPlayer.UI -c Debug) succeeded; full `dotnet test` suite green (812 tests, up from 810 — the two new FEAT-003 tests added and passing). No bin/obj clean/delete; the three real ServiceOrders JSONs stay intact.

MODIFIED: WorshipPlayer.Presenter\Views\OperatorWindow.xaml.cs
  - ADDED `private bool TryOpenSlideServiceItemEditor(ServiceItem item)`: returns false (fall back to AddServiceItemDialog) when item.Type != ServiceItemType.Slides, when _serviceOrderManager?.CurrentServiceOrder is null, or when any of _slidePresentationService/_mediaLibraryService/_templateService is null. Otherwise constructs `new SlideServiceItemEditorWindow(item, _serviceOrderManager.CurrentServiceOrder.Items, _slidePresentationService, _mediaLibraryService, _templateService) { Owner = this }`, subscribes `win.RemoveRequested += (_, __) => { removed = true; win.DialogResult = false; win.Close(); }` (local bool removed=false), then `bool saved = win.ShowDialog() == true;`. After ShowDialog it runs the flow on Dispatcher.InvokeAsync (async): removed -> IndexOf + RemoveItem; else !saved -> return (discard); else the window already copied back; then `await SaveServiceOrderAsync(); await PrimeSlidePresentationCacheAsync(); RefreshServiceOrderList(); RefreshSlideSections();` (wrapped in try/catch -> ShowToolError). Returns true.
  - Branched Slides out of BOTH edit entry points: `if (TryOpenSlideServiceItemEditor(display.Item)) return;` at the top of EditSelectedServiceItem() (after the null/display.Item==null guards, before AddServiceItemDialog), and `if (TryOpenSlideServiceItemEditor(item)) return;` at the top of EditServiceItemDirect(item). OpenSelectedItemSettings and every non-Slides path unchanged; non-Slides items still open AddServiceItemDialog.
  (No new usings needed — WorshipPlayer.Presenter.Views.Slides was already imported.)

MODIFIED: WorshipPlayer.Tests\SlideServiceItemEditorModelTests.cs — extended (not duplicated; FEAT-001 already covered the mirror + SpecificItem/GoToItemId) with:
  - HostSavePath_SlidesItem_RoundTripsThroughJsonFile: a Slides item with all additive fields (SlidePresentationId, BackgroundType=Video, MediaPath, MediaType=Video, TransitionTimeMs=1200, AudioAttachments, AudioAttachmentPath, StageTemplateId) + AutoAdvanceSettings {AfterCondition=Timer, GoTo=SpecificItem, GoToItemId, TransitionFadeTimeMs} saved via ServiceOrderManager.SaveAsync then reloaded from the authoritative JSON FILE by a FRESH manager (the UI 'restart'); asserts every field equal incl. the SpecificItem/GoToItemId when-complete destination.
  - RealServiceOrderFiles_StillDeserializeWithoutError: walks up from AppContext.BaseDirectory to find the worktree's ServiceOrders folder, copies each real/demo JSON into a temp ServiceOrders folder (throwaway app.db — no runtime data touched), and asserts ServiceOrderManager.LoadAsync returns non-null with non-null Items for each. No-ops if the folder/sample files are absent. Found + loaded all three: 2026-08-03_Sunday Morning.json, Sunday Morning Demo.json, TheBlessing Service.json.

NOTE: the CS4014 warning at OperatorWindow.xaml.cs line 710 is PRE-EXISTING (the existing PrimeSlidePresentationCacheAsync dispatcher call), not from this change. The 'Error loading service order' line in test output is an existing negative-path test with deliberately malformed JSON (logged + swallowed), not a failure.
